Methodology + working calculators. Week 11 fair lines are TBD until QIA blockers clear — this page explains how lines will be originated, not what they will be. The calculator below is illustrative only.
• Spread: Handicap on margin. Favorite −X must win by more than X; underdog +X covers by losing by less or winning. Whole-number spread can push (refund); half-point cannot.
• Moneyline: Straight winner, margin irrelevant. Minus = favorite (risk to win $100); plus = underdog (win per $100).
• Total (O/U): Combined points vs number. Whole-number total can push; half-point cannot.

• Price vs number: The number (e.g. −3.5) and the price (−110) are separate. Standard spread price −110/−110 implies 52.38% each (104.76% total) — the extra ~4.76% is the book’s vig/hold. A line is a price to balance risk, not a score prediction. Sources: GamblingSite — How to Read NFL Odds · OddsShopper — Implied Probability.
No-vig (fair) prob = implied / sum(implied)    e.g. 52.38/104.76 = 50.00% each (≈ +100)
Expected value per unit staked:  EV = p·b − (1−p)   where b = net odds (decimal − 1)
Kelly fraction: f* = (b·p − q) / b, q = 1−p (maximizes log-growth; use fractional Kelly in practice)

A competition where strategies earn rewards for repeatable, validated edge — not for one hot week. Every strategy must pass the gates below before it can rank. Performance cells are blank until a strategy actually passes; we do not invent win rates.

How ranking works (proposed — see S-04): Rank by out-of-sample closing-line value (CLV) + ROI with minimum sample size, not by raw win rate. A strategy that beats the closing line consistently is showing skill; one that only wins in-sample is showing luck.
G1 · Pre-registrationStrategy rules frozen before the test window (no tuning on the test set)Written spec + timestampStops hindsight fitting
G2 · Minimum sampleEnough bets to separate skill from noise≥ 200 bets (single-bet strategies); ≥ 100 tickets (parlays)Small samples are dominated by variance
G3 · Out-of-sample testTest on a later season/week block never used for designSeparate train / validation / test splitsProves the edge travels
G4 · Closing-line valueAverage price vs closing line (your number vs close)Positive CLV on averageBeating the close is the cleanest skill signal
G5 · ROI with costsROI after vig, with confidence interval95% CI excludes 0 (or report CI honestly)Prevents “profitable” noise from ranking
G6 · Correlation checkLegs/signals not secretly the same bet (see below)Pairwise |r| reported; correlated legs penalisedParlays/props often double-count one outcome
G7 · StabilityEdge holds across home/away, spread/total, early/late seasonNo single split drives all profitOne matchup type ≠ a strategy

Parlay rule: legs must be independent enough (G6). A same-game parlay whose legs all need the same script (e.g. QB over + WR over + team total over) is one correlated bet, not three edges. Price every ticket against the no-vig fair price of its legs.

Prop rule: start from role (snaps / routes / targets / carries), then efficiency, then opponent + game script. A prop line is a projection threshold near the middle of the expected range with a price attached — see methodology notes on Sources. Combos must pass the same correlation gate as parlays.

High |r| ⇒ legs are not independent ⇒ parlay fair price must use the joint probability, not the product of marginals.

Correlation ≠ causation. A strong r between “QB throws a lot” and “WR catches a lot” does not prove either causes the other — both may be driven by game script (trailing). Always check n, out-of-sample stability, and the football mechanism before building a combo.
• Report n, ROI, and 95% confidence interval — never win rate alone.
• Show CLV vs the closing line; a strategy that cannot beat the close has not shown skill.
• Split results by home/away, favorite/underdog, and month — flag any split that flips sign.
• Disclose every parameter tuned and the exact test window. Undisclosed tuning = disqualified.
• For parlays/props: publish leg correlations and the joint fair price, not just the ticket price.
